item.title: Packers' interest in Jonathan Taylor shows desire to move on from Josh Jacobs and his domestic abuse issues
item.description: The Green Bay Packers' pursuit of Jonathan Taylor a sign Josh Jacobs' days in Green Bay seem numbered amid expanding domestic abuse allegations.
item.content:encoded:
Jonathan Taylor's almost certain trade from the Indianapolis Colts by the NFL's Nov. 10 trade deadline comes with a multitude of subplots but none more gripping than the interest the Green Bay Packers have in the running back and what that means.

The Packers' interest, at whatever level that has reached, shows the team's willingness to move on from Pro Bowl running back Josh Jacobs, who is currently on their roster but has been a disappointment and something of a headaches because of his legal problems.

It has been widely reported, and confirmed by OutKick and Fox News Digital that the Packers are among the teams that have expressed varying degrees of interest in trading for Taylor – a list that includes the Denver Broncos, Minnesota Vikings, New York Giants and, yes, the Packers.

PACKERS ACTIVATE JOSH JACOBS; RUNNING BACK SET TO PLAY IN FIRST GAME SINCE DOMESTIC VIOLENCE ARREST

And while the interest from the other teams is generally tied to a desire get consistent production in their running game, the Packers' interest glows in neon because Jacobs' days with the Packers seem numbered.

Jacobs, 28, has played in two games for Green Bay this season after spending the first six games on the Commissioner’s Exempt List — which is effectively a paid suspension.

That time on the list followed Jacobs pleading no contest in September to battery and criminal-damage-to-property charges stemming from a May domestic incident with his former girlfriend.

But Jacobs remains under serious NFL scrutiny as the league said Saturday it is reviewing previously unreported allegations that Jacobs physically abused three other women.

That review expanded after police records released Oct. 30 showed that the three other women had contacted authorities about alleged physical or verbal abuse by Jacobs in incidents dating to 2021.

Jacobs’ attorneys David Z. Chesnoff, Richard A. Schonfeld, and Clarence F. Duchac III, released a statement Saturday addressing the allegations by saying police had weighed the allegations from the three other women and moved forward with "only two misdemeanor charges."

But that is not the point.

The point is an NFL suspension under the Personal Conduct Policy is in the works and now could include newfound allegations of abuse.

And regardless of when that suspension comes, the new allegations are a black eye against Jacobs and the Packers by extension for continuing to support a player who carries an expanding list of domestic abuse allegations.

JOSH JACOBS FACES TWO MISDEMEANORS CHARGERS AFTER STRANGULATION ARREST AND PACKERS PREPARE FOR ANY SCENARIO

So would the Packers be better off with Jonathan Taylor, who is among the league's rushing leaders and is tied for league lead with eight rushing touchdowns? Or would they be prefer to continue carrying Jacobs and his uncertain playing status upon completion of the NFL's Personal Conduct Policy Review?

These are not tough questions. And the Packers' apparent interest in Taylor has already delivered an answer.

The greater problem here is whether the Packers would be willing to pay the heavy price to acquire Taylor. The Colts want a deal founded on the Christian McCaffrey trade of 2022 between the Carolina Panthers and San Francisco 49ers.

The Niners sent Carolina a second-, third-, and fourth-round pick in 2023 and a fifth-rounder in 2024.

COLTS TRADE PRO BOWL GUARD QUENTON NELSON TO SEAHAWKS, THE FIRST OF WHAT COULD BE MULTIPLE DEADLINE MOVES

If the Packers are willing to pay that price, the jettisoning of Jacobs and his domestic abuse ties seem uncomplicated by comparison.

The Packers could actually trigger in the neighborhood of $5 million in salary cap savings by releasing Jacobs by the trade deadline.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

And while there is a dead cap charge the team would have to absorb the remainder of this year and next, the cap savings for 2027, the final year of Jacobs' contract, would be around $13 million.

The math makes sense. The upgrade at the position makes sense. The relief of what has become a growing legal headache makes sense.

The Packers' interest in Jonathan Taylor makes sense in context of moving on from Josh Jacobs.

item.title: Fake party invite scam: Can you trust a friend's reply?
item.description: A phishing email disguised as an Evite fooled a man even after he emailed his friend to verify it, revealing how compromised Gmail accounts aid scams.
item.content:encoded:
An invitation from a friend lands in your inbox. Something feels off, so you do the responsible thing. You email your friend to make sure the invitation is legitimate. A reply comes back confirming everything. You would probably feel comfortable clicking at that point, right?

That's what makes a recent email from John in Westlake, Ohio, so unsettling. He received a suspicious Evite and decided to investigate. However, the response he received raised even more questions. John has since confirmed with his friend that the emails were part of a scam. His experience reveals a potential weakness in how we verify suspicious emails, especially when someone else's inbox may be compromised.

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.

Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

FAKE CHATGPT BILLING EMAILS CAN STEAL YOUR LOGIN

John received what appeared to be a fraudulent Evite from a friend. After reading our previous warnings about fake Evite emails, he decided to email his friend directly rather than click the invitation. What happened next made him even more suspicious.

Here's what John wrote:

"I received what I thought was a fraudulent eVite from a friend. Thanks to your previous posts, I strongly suspected that this was a phishing attempt. So, I independently emailed my friend and asked if the eVite was legitimate. I got the response below."

Hi John

This is from me, and I sent it, Sorry for the confusion,

Thank you

"It appears that the scammers either set up an auto-response on the Gmail account or manually responded to my email. The punctuation was wrong, so I didn't consider the response legitimate."

John thought the reply sounded unlike his friend and wondered whether someone had gained access to the account. He later contacted his friend again and confirmed that the emails were a scam. John also shared the actual Evite-branded invitation, which advertised a "Dinner Gathering & Celebration" and included a "View Invitation" button. Its polished design resembled a legitimate event invitation, showing how easily someone could mistake a fraudulent message for the real thing.

WHY VERIFIED SOCIAL MEDIA ACCOUNTS CAN STILL LEAD YOU INTO A SCAM

Most people know they should be cautious about unexpected links. In fact, we've repeatedly encouraged readers to verify suspicious messages before taking action. That remains excellent advice. However, there's an additional concern when the email account you're contacting may already be under someone else's control.

The Federal Trade Commission warned in May 2026 about fraudulent invitations that imitate popular services such as Evite and Paperless Post. These messages may appear to come from someone you recognize. When you try to view the invitation, a fake website can ask for your email password or a verification code.

If criminals obtain access to that account, they may send more fraudulent invitations to the account owner's contacts. The messages can appear to originate from a legitimate email address, making them especially convincing. Now consider what happens when someone replies to one of those invitations asking whether it's real. If a criminal still controls the sender's inbox, that person could potentially intercept the question and send a reassuring answer. A recipient might then believe the invitation is safe because a familiar email address confirmed it.

John wondered whether someone had configured an automatic response inside his friend's Gmail account. Technically, that's possible. Gmail allows users to create email templates and filters that automatically respond to certain messages. Someone with unauthorized access could potentially misuse that feature or simply respond manually while impersonating the account owner.

Although John confirmed the emails were fraudulent, we still don't know how the reassuring reply was generated. There's no technical evidence yet showing whether someone accessed his friend's account, configured an automatic response or used another method to impersonate him. What John's experience does demonstrate is that a reassuring email reply can accompany a confirmed scam.

We reached out to Evite about John's experience and asked whether the company was aware of this type of scam. In a statement provided to CyberGuy, Evite said:

"We're not currently seeing a rise in phishing scams, however, staying aware is always important, which is why we're constantly monitoring and providing tools to help users spot the fakes at evite.com/blog/etiquette/how-to-spot-phishing-email-scam/ . The best way to tell the difference is that a scam is generic, but a real gathering today is highly specific. Real hosts are over-communicating, sharing everything from parking instructions and dress codes to very specific themes like 'Strawberry' or 'Western.' That level of detail is what makes a modern invite harder to fake and gives guests the confidence to say 'yes' without second-guessing.

Evite advice? Check the details. If it just says 'You're invited' with a link, be cautious. A real Evite host today is telling you where to park and what to wear."

Evite's advice is worth keeping in mind, although scammers can also create convincing invitations with specific event details. That's why it's important to take additional precautions before clicking an unexpected invitation.

A few changes to how you verify unexpected invitations can help prevent a suspicious email from becoming a much bigger problem.

If an invitation seems unusual, contact the sender using a phone number you already have. You can also reach out through another established communication channel, provided you have reason to trust that account. Avoid using phone numbers included in the suspicious invitation. A criminal could provide a fake contact number designed to make the story sound legitimate.

Be cautious if an invitation asks you to enter your email password or share a security code before revealing event details. A phishing website may use those requests to steal account access. If you expect an invitation from a particular service, open its official app or visit its website directly. Check whether the invitation appears in your account rather than following an unfamiliar link.

Pay attention if a familiar contact suddenly uses an unusual writing style or gives an answer that doesn't fit the conversation. Unexpected requests to click another link should make you even more cautious. However, don't rely entirely on spelling mistakes or punctuation. Criminals can write convincing messages, while legitimate emails may contain errors. The safest approach is to confirm the situation through another trusted method.

Fake invitations can sometimes lead to malicious downloads rather than stolen passwords. In certain attacks, criminals disguise remote access software as something you need to install to view an invitation. Strong antivirus software can help identify dangerous downloads and block known malicious websites on supported devices. Keep your operating system and security software updated so you receive the latest available protections. If you accidentally downloaded an invitation file, avoid opening it. Run a security scan using trusted software. If you entered login credentials on a suspicious website, change them through the legitimate service immediately. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android & iOS devices at Cyberguy.com

If you suspect someone has accessed your Gmail account, review its settings for changes you didn't make. An attacker may use forwarding or automated email rules to interfere with incoming messages.

On a computer, follow these steps:

If you discover unfamiliar settings, investigate them and remove unauthorized changes. You should also secure your Google account and review recent sign-in activity.

A strong, unique password helps protect your email. You should also enable two-factor authentication or use a passkey where supported. Passkeys provide stronger protection against phishing because they are tied to legitimate websites or apps. Visit your Google Account security settings at myaccount.google.com/security to review recent activity and connected devices. If you suspect unauthorized access, change your password using a trusted device and sign out unfamiliar sessions. A password manager can help you avoid reusing passwords across accounts. That way, one exposed password is less likely to compromise another service.

Scammers often use personal information found online to make fraudulent messages sound more convincing. Data brokers collect and sell details such as your email address, phone number and information about your family. A personal data removal service can help reduce that exposure by requesting that participating data brokers remove your information. Although no service can erase everything or prevent a friend's email account from being hacked, limiting what's available online may make it harder for criminals to personalize scams. Check out my top picks for data removal services and get a free scan to find out if your personal information is already out on the web by visiting Cyberguy.com

When you encounter a fraudulent invitation, use your email provider's phishing-reporting tools. In Gmail, open the suspicious message, select the three-dot menu and choose Report phishing . You can also report scams to the Federal Trade Commission at ReportFraud.ftc.gov. If the message appears to come from a friend, contact that person using another trusted channel. They may need to secure their account and alert other people who received similar invitations.

If your friend confirms that someone accessed their account, avoid interacting with the invitation. Save the suspicious message as evidence and report it to your email provider. You may also want to check whether you received any follow-up messages containing unfamiliar links.

Encourage your friend to begin account recovery through their email provider's official website. They should review their account activity and remove unauthorized access. If the scammer sent invitations to other contacts, your friend should warn those people through a communication method they still control. For Gmail users, Google provides instructions for securing a hacked account. Acting quickly may help prevent additional messages from reaching trusted contacts.

John's email made me reconsider a piece of advice I often give. I've always encouraged people to contact someone they know when a suspicious message arrives. I still believe that's smart advice, but how you reach that person is important. If their email account has been compromised, you could end up communicating with the scammer instead. Personally, I'd rather pick up the phone and call a number I already trust. I'm glad John trusted his instincts and followed up with his friend. He received a reply saying the invitation was legitimate, yet he kept questioning it. That extra effort helped him confirm the scam. We can't assume every strangely worded email comes from a hacker, but we also shouldn't ignore something that feels wrong. Scammers count on us trusting familiar names and email addresses. John's experience shows why a little extra verification can be worth the effort.

Have you ever questioned a suspicious email, only to receive a reassuring reply that still didn't sound like the person you knew? Did you later discover their account had been hacked? I'd like to hear what happened so write to us at Cyberguy.com

item.content:encoded:
I'm back from vacation and in need of a vacation from the vacation. I spent a good part of the day yesterday in the car and missed a lot of college football action trying to make it back in time for our little guy to go trick or treating.

That was a success and, after I unpacked, I was able to catch the unranked Tar Heels and a single and focused Bill Belichick nearly upset No. 1 Miami. Bill and company almost pulled it off.

Everyone knows it only really counts if you pull it off. Which brings me to another of the games I caught the end of, unranked USC defeating No. 2-ranked Ohio State. Obviously, the Buckeyes were once again highly overrated.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

You hate to see Ohio State lose a game on the road that they should win. Sadly, you're going to hear all kinds of excuses about Julian Sayin being injured. Bottom line, they couldn't get the job done. The beard dye is fading in Columbus.

Now to more important matters than the sad state of Ohio State football. Paige Spiranac putting her love of Halloween on display for all of America.

If you're going to do such a thing, you have to go all out.

It's safe to say that the top golf influencer on the planet, and some are even saying the best influencer to have ever done it, went all out.

PAIGE SPIRANAC GIVES PEOPLE WHAT THEY DIDN'T KNOW THEY NEEDED: HER YOGURT BOWL RECIPE

Are we still declaring winners of Halloween and other holidays?

I don't know. I'm never on top of those sorts of things. Although I do strongly believe in recognizing greatness.

Paige's effort here is unmatched. The numbers speak for themselves. She showed up and kept the pressure on everyone else trying to compete.

If that's not how you win Halloween, I don't know the rules anymore.

I watched the "Capturing Bigfoot" documentary when it came out on Bigfoot Day, which is October 20, for those who didn't know.

The documentary is about the famous 1967 Patterson-Gimlin Bigfoot footage. The footage that supposedly shows Bigfoot out for a stroll in California.

There were a few things about the Patterson-Gimlin film that I didn’t know before I sat down and watched it. On the top of that list is that people still believed, at least before this documentary, that footage was real.

That blew me away. I thought it was agreed upon long ago that it was fake. Apparently not. There were some out there who believed it was real video evidence of Bigfoot.

The documentary (spoiler alert) shows another piece of footage that was believed to be a test run a year before Roger Patterson and Robert Gimlin filmed the footage we have all seen.

I debated whether I would write a standalone article about the documentary and I decided that it belonged in "America's Best Daily Column." I said in a prior edition of Sunday Screencaps that I would watch it after all, and I did purchase it and waste my time watching it.

CARMEN ELECTRA OFFICIALLY KICKS OFF HALLOWEEN SEASON AT A GAS STATION, POSTGAME POLICE CHASE & BALL-SAC

Back to the doc. Another piece of information I learned about the Patterson-Gimlin film was how much money it generated when it first came out. I had no idea that it was shown in venues around the country.

I didn’t get into Bigfoot because of the Patterson-Gimlin film.

As I've mentioned before, it was the fine work and incredible confidence in the existence of Bigfoot (despite an overwhelming lack of evidence) by the folks on the show "Finding Bigfoot" that got me hooked.

So, if you're interested in learning more about the Patterson-Gimlin film, the documentary will fill you in. They spoke to many people involved in and around the famous footage.

If you're hoping this documentary finally debunks the Patterson-Gimlin film, I'd point you at the original footage. That does a decent job of debunking it all by itself.

Oh, and one more thing I learned from this doc. The Bigfoot in the Patterson-Gimlin is female and has boobs.

item.title: Ancient Roman treasure unearthed at military base, two coins aren't what they seem
item.description: The Roman coin hoard on Gotland features five emperors and four empresses from the second century A.D., but two coins may be ancient fakes from Ukraine.
item.content:encoded:
Archaeologists in Sweden recently made an unusual discovery. They found 45 ancient Roman silver coins, including two believed to be counterfeits.

The discovery was announced by the Swedish Armed Forces earlier this fall.

The coins were unearthed during archaeological excavations ahead of an expansion of Sweden's Gotland Regiment military base, according to officials.

MYSTERIOUS FIND BENEATH FIELD LEADS MAN TO MASSIVE TREASURE HIDDEN FOR CENTURIES

"During one of the excavations, an unusual find was made — a silver treasure with Roman coins from the second century A.D.," the Swedish Armed Forces said in a translated statement.

The discovery came as archaeologists were wrapping up an excavation of a farmhouse foundation dating to the Migration Period, which spanned roughly the fifth and sixth centuries A.D.

The archaeologists were making "one final sweep with the metal detector" before the discovery, according to officials.

"Then an insistent beeping indicated that something was in the ground near one of the foundation stones," the statement said. 

"They carefully dug a small silver coin out of the soil — and more finds would follow."

RARE COIN BEARING FACE OF KING WITH INFAMOUS NICKNAME UNEARTHED AFTER 1,000 YEARS

When archaeologists brushed off the coin, they discovered a stamped portrait of Roman Emperor Antoninus Pius, who ruled from 138 to 161 A.D.

"The metal detector's persistent beeping indicated that more objects were hidden near the same foundation stone," officials said.

"Before the workday was over, archaeologists had counted 45 coins and a gold finger ring. All the coins are Roman, minted during the second century for five emperors and four empresses."

The coins were identified by Lennart Lind, a Swedish expert on Roman coins.

ARCHAEOLOGISTS UNCOVER SPRAWLING ROMAN ESTATE BURIED FOR CENTURIES BENEATH FARMLAND

The coins feature five Roman emperors — Trajan, Hadrian, Antoninus Pius, Marcus Aurelius and Commodus — as well as four empresses: Vibia Sabina, Faustina I, Faustina II and Lucilla, according to officials.

Experts believe the coins arrived on Gotland during the fourth century and were used in trade for generations before being buried alongside the gold ring around 450 A.D.

Two of the coins, however, were ancient counterfeits that may have originated in what is now Ukraine, according to archaeologists.

Elsewhere on the military grounds, archaeologists found nine graves believed to be around 2,000 years old, including one containing nearly 10 pounds of burned human bones, according to the release.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

The remains belonged to at least two individuals, including an adult man, officials said.

Archaeologists also discovered bronze fittings believed to have been attached to a sword suspension and a shield.

The coins may have been buried as part of a sacrifice, said Per Widerström, an archaeologist at Gotland Museum.

Widerström told Fox News Digital the silver coins were largely what archaeologists would expect to uncover at such a site, but the gold ring was unusual.

Widerström also said newly received radiocarbon dating results indicated activity at the settlement from the fourth through sixth centuries, consistent with archaeologists' expectations.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

"Perhaps it was abandoned around 540 when there was a low in human history in this part of the world because of natural disasters from 536 A.D. and on for 10 years," Widerström said. "Maybe that is the reason behind them leaving the farm."

The bigger surprise, he said, was the number of buildings identified at the site — six in total, apparently belonging to two neighboring farms.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"It looks like it was slowly abandoned, and some of the people might even have come back to this place to get more things back to a new settlement," he said.

The Roman coin hoard is the latest in a series of ancient discoveries in Sweden.

Earlier this year, Swedish archaeologists discovered two rare Bronze Age neck rings believed to be more than 2,500 years old buried inside an ancient grave monument.

Last winter, Swedish officials announced the discovery of an exceptionally well-preserved, 5,000-year-old dog skeleton buried alongside a bone dagger near Stockholm.

item.title: Why people really stopped having kids: New study uncovers the surprising reasons families are shrinking
item.description: A new Institute for Family Studies report reveals how cultural forces like peer support, pet parenting and modern anxiety shape family planning beyond housing costs.
item.content:encoded:
High housing costs and unequal chore loads may not fully explain the drop in birth rates around the world, according to a new report from the Institute for Family Studies and the Wheatley Institute.

The survey of nearly 10,000 respondents across more than a dozen countries points to culture, finding that peer pressure, anxiety about the future and the rise of "pet parenting" strongly influence whether couples choose to start or grow a family.

"Ultra-Orthodox Jews in Brooklyn have six kids each. Their hipster neighbors have 1.6 kids each," Lyman Stone, senior fellow and director of the Pronatalism Initiative at the Institute for Family Studies, told Fox News Digital. "They live in the same economy. They have very different outcomes. Why? Different culture."

AGE OF FIRST-TIME MOTHERS HITS RECORD HIGH IN BLUE STATES AS BIRTH RATES KEEP FALLING

The report also tested whether sharing chores affects fertility intentions, finding no statistically significant relationship between family planning and either the division of household responsibilities or perceptions of fairness.

"There's been a lot of research on, you know, 'If men did more laundry, would birth rates go up? If men helped out more at home, would birth rates go up?' And the answer is basically no," Stone said.

ALEX BERENSON: GENTLE PARENTING CAN'T REPLACE THE STRENGTH OF A GOOD DAD

"The last 30 years have seen a revolution in involved fatherhood. Dads are doing more at home than ever before and fertility rates keep plummeting," he added to Fox News Digital.

One of the strongest associations researchers identified was between fertility intentions and having a supportive circle of friends. Believing that one's friends would celebrate a new baby was linked to a 10% increase in desired family size and a 20% higher likelihood of intending to have another child.

TRADITIONAL TWO-PARENT FAMILIES VANISH FROM BIG AMERICAN CITIES AS 'MARRIAGE DESERTS' EXPAND

"All around the world, we just found that friends are really important," Stone said. "Where peer culture ratifies and encourages family life, family life is more successful."

The association extended beyond friends to admired public figures. Respondents who admired a celebrity with more children than they had were 14% more likely to intend to have another child.

DRIVEN BY PROGRESSIVE DOOMISM, LIBERALS ARE HAVING FEWER BABIES THAN CONSERVATIVE FAMILIES

Researchers also identified a connection between attitudes toward pets and decisions about having children. Respondents who expressed a preference for being a "pet parent" rather than having children reported a 30% lower desired family size and showed a 50% drop in intentions to have more children.

"The animal is not the problem. The problem is the attitude," Stone said. "That says that, you know, changing a litter box is truly as meaningful as changing a diaper. And I just have to tell you, it isn't."

AMERICA’S BABY BUST MAY BE LINKED TO THE IPHONE, STUDY SAYS

Researchers found that risk aversion, anxiety about the future and general pessimism were also associated with smaller desired families. Respondents who were more comfortable taking risks and optimistic about their futures tended to desire and have more children.

"Some decline in fertility may just be because there's bad vibes," Stone said to Fox News Digital. "There's just the internet constantly telling you that everything is bad, everything's getting worse and there’s a million things to be worried about and you shouldn't take any risks."

"I hate to tell you, but yeah, having children has a possibility of hurting you, both physically, financially and emotionally, in the long run, you know, a child who grows up to reject you is a very painful thing. So yes, there is risk with having kids. But there is also great reward," he added.

Encouragement from parents was another significant factor associated with fertility intentions. According to the study, "Parental encouragement to have children is associated with an 11% increase in desired number of children and a 30% increase in the likelihood of intending to have another one." Encouraging childless, cohabiting adult children to marry was also associated with a 14% higher likelihood of intending to have a child.

FAMILY BREAKDOWN IN PENNSYLVANIA PROMPTS FAITH-BASED EFFORT TO BRING MARRIAGE BACK

But Stone cautioned that guilt-tripping adult children into having kids may be ineffective. Instead, he suggested parents share the joy they experienced raising children and offer practical support.

"If you're a parent and you want grandbabies from your adult children, you probably won't get very far telling them that they owe you grandbabies," Stone said. "But you may get somewhere telling them stories of how much you enjoyed raising them and how much fun you think you're going to have helping them raise their children."

NEW STUDY REVEALS THE SINGLE MOST CRITICAL FACTOR IN WHETHER CHILDREN KEEP THEIR FAITH INTO ADULTHOOD

Religion was another factor linked to larger families. Respondents with the highest levels of religious devotion had 9% more children and were 12% more likely to intend to have another child.

But researchers found no statistically significant relationship between hearing clergy speak about family and family size. Instead, the findings suggest religious communities may be associated with fertility intentions through friendships and networks of practical support, including help with meals and celebrating the arrival of a new baby.

"Where religion really does matter is it shapes the friendships people have. Religious people were overwhelmingly more likely to have friends who would be supportive of them having kids," Stone said.

"So, it seems that what's going on is religious communities are religious communities. They are places where people form friendships that create bonds of mutual support that exist almost secondary to the doctrines and theology of the organization. And first and foremost are about mutual investment in one another," he added.

For Stone, the findings suggest that efforts to encourage family formation do not depend solely on government policies or financial incentives. Friends, relatives and neighbors can also play a role by creating communities where raising children is supported and encouraged.

"You matter to the people around you and you have influence on them," Stone said. "You don't have to wait for the government to pass a law to make a difference for family formation. Regular people can influence this just by being good friends, good neighbors, good parents, good leaders and good members of the community, and telling young families: 'We're here for you, we support you, we think this is a good and admirable thing to do.'"

item.title: Trump's DOJ makeover hasn't changed where the political cash is flowing — and the gap is growing
item.description: Over 75% of Department of Justice employee donations still go to Democratic committees despite Trump administration efforts to root out partisan bias.
item.content:encoded:
The Trump administration has sought to eliminate what it alleges is partisan bias within the Justice Department, but the vast majority of political donations from individuals identifying themselves as DOJ employees are still going to Democratic-aligned committees, according to a Fox News Digital analysis of federal campaign finance records.

Between January 2025 and August of this year, just over 75% of campaign contributions from individuals identifying themselves as Department of Justice employees went to Democratic committees, the analysis of federal campaign finance records found.

Fox News Digital analyzed roughly $300,000 in political contributions recorded by the Federal Election Commission between January 2025 and August 2026 from donors who listed their employer as "Department of Justice," "DOJ" or a variation of those names. Contributions were categorized by the political affiliation of the recipient candidate or committee, while independent-expenditure committees were classified according to the candidates or parties they supported. When exporting data from the Federal Election Commission's dashboard, an option to include donations from "unique individuals only" was selected to filter out duplicative records.

As the Trump administration has progressed, the partisan slant of DOJ donations has become more pronounced. Through 2025, about 70% of donations from those identifying themselves as DOJ staff went to Democratic committees, a figure that rose to just under 90% in 2026, according to Fox News Digital's findings.

TODD BLANCHE EXPOSES HOW AGGRESSIVE BIDEN DOJ TARGETED LOW-LEVEL MAR-A-LAGO EMPLOYEES

Attorney General Todd Blanche and his predecessor, Pam Bondi, both claimed that the Trump administration inherited a deeply corrupt DOJ, pointing to allegations that the agency was inundated with political bias under President Joe Biden's tenure.

"There are a lot of people in the FBI and also in the Department of Justice who despise Donald Trump, despise us," Bondi said in early 2025. "Right now, we’re going to root them out; we will find them, and they will no longer be employed."

Critics have pushed back against claims of political weaponization during the Biden administration, arguing that high-profile investigations into President Donald Trump and other conservatives originated from legitimate legal concerns.

DOJ DANGLES MASSIVE SIGNING BONUSES FOR LAWYERS READY TO FIGHT ‘LAWLESS’ CITIES FAR BEYOND DC

Both of Trump’s attorneys general under his second administration have made strides to recruit a greater number of ideologically aligned lawyers while attempting to push those out who may not be willing to advance the administration’s interests.

In early February 2026, DOJ chief of staff Chad Mizelle publicly encouraged lawyers who "support President Trump" to contact him about becoming federal prosecutors. Stephen Miller amplified the appeal on social media with the caption "patriots needed," and sitting U.S. Attorney Jason Quiñones reposted the appeal alongside the phrase "we are hiring!" Mizelle later defended the approach as ensuring that executive-branch lawyers were in line with the elected president’s agenda.

LEGAL WAR ON TRUMP’S AGENDA GAINS FIREPOWER AS FEDERAL LAWYERS DEFECT TO DEMOCRATS

The administration's personnel overhaul has coincided with a substantial exodus of attorneys from federal service.

Over 10,000 attorneys have left federal service since Trump took office for a second term.

Fox News Digital reported in July that well over 100 federal attorneys had left the Trump administration for roles in Democratic-run state attorneys general offices. Many of these lawyers took decades of experience with them, prompting concerns that the Trump administration could be depriving itself of the ability to handle highly technical legal matters.

Some of these seasoned former federal lawyers have since joined legal action against the Trump administration.

While a significant number of government lawyers have left federal service under Trump, and some prominent conservatives have joined the administration, campaign finance records show that Democratic committees continue to receive the overwhelming majority of political contributions from donors identifying themselves as Justice Department employees.

Among the most common recipients of donations from those identifying themselves as DOJ employees were Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., Sen. Jon Ossoff, D-Georgia, and Emily’s List, a pro-abortion group associated with the Democratic Party. Some conservative committees, such as those in Trump’s network of PACs, were also common targets for Justice Department donors.

DEMOCRAT POLITICOS RERUN UNDERHANDED LEFTIST PLAYBOOK IN EFFORT TO TORPEDO TRUMP’S AG NOMINEE

Much of the DOJ's work concerns investigations and prosecutions unrelated to partisan politics, and the campaign finance records do not establish whether employees' political preferences have influenced the department's day-to-day operations.

Progressive critics, to the contrary, have alleged that the Trump administration is using the Justice Department to target its political enemies.

"Those who were fired from the Department were fired for a reason. Those who resigned or took the fork in the road option likely aligned more with the priorities of President Biden and would naturally leave, which is common during transitions," a DOJ spokeswoman previously told Fox News Digital. "The Administration gave career employees the fork in the road option to intentionally reduce the size of the government and eliminate unnecessary layers of staff who don’t effectively contribute to the mission of aggressively tackling crime."

The DOJ did not respond to a request for comment when reached by Fox News Digital on Monday.

item.title: ‘Baywatch’ beauty Erika Eleniak on pace for $1 million OnlyFans payday decades after iconic TV role
item.description: Erika Eleniak reportedly earned nearly $300,000 in three months on OnlyFans and is set to reprise her role in Fox's upcoming "Baywatch" reboot in 2027.
item.content:encoded:

Eleniak played lifeguard Shauni McClain on "Baywatch" from 1989 to 1992, becoming one of the show's original stars.

‘AMERICAN PIE’ ALUM SHANNON ELIZABETH TURNS TO ONLYFANS FOR ‘FRESH START’ AS DIVORCE UNFOLDS

"When I first thought about joining OnlyFans, I honestly believed I was going to hate it," Eleniak told Fox News Digital. "But I have to tell you, I absolutely love it. It has given me this incredible opportunity to reconnect with so many wonderful people who have followed my career since the 1980s, from 'E.T.' to 'Baywatch,' my Playboy days, 'The Beverly Hillbillies,' and everything in between."

"I never imagined that joining OnlyFans would have such an emotional impact on me," she admitted. "For the first time in my life, I genuinely feel loved, appreciated and empowered in a way I never have before. It's an extraordinary feeling, and I honestly can't believe how much happiness it's brought into my life."

"I'm embracing this new chapter with open arms, and I feel more confident, more connected and more excited about the future than I have in years," Eleniak added.

According to TMZ, Eleniak is making "far more" than the $10,000 per week she was reportedly earning shortly after launching her profile in August. The outlet previously reported that Eleniak had more than 1,100 subscribers.

"What has touched me the most is realizing just how many people have stayed with me throughout all these years," Eleniak told Fox News Digital. "Some have been there since the very beginning, and now we're reconnecting in such a personal and meaningful way. I cannot begin to express how grateful I am to every single one of them. They're the reason I've had the career I've had, and they've given me so much love and support throughout my life."

OnlyFans allows creators, including celebrities, athletes and sex workers, to charge subscribers directly for content. The platform has attracted hundreds of millions of users and generated billions of dollars in annual transactions, according to company financial figures.

Eleniak said she initially joined OnlyFans because she thought it would be a fun way to connect with fans. She previously told Fox News Digital that she sometimes felt insecure while filming "Baywatch" in a swimsuit, but said she now feels more comfortable in her own skin.

"Well, that didn't change," she said. "When you're working in a costume that's basically a bathing suit, and you're running and doing action and all kinds of things, it's not the most comfortable uniform on the planet. So I don't think that would change for me today. But I am 57 years old. I am comfortable in my body and in my skin. I love where I'm at right now. So I suppose that's changed."

Eleniak describes her content as "personal, playful and unfiltered." She also isn't afraid to dip her toes into some unusual requests.

Eleniak said she has faced little backlash since joining OnlyFans.

"I've been pleasantly surprised," she explained. "I've had a really warm welcome, and a lot of cheering on from people just saying, 'Go get it, have fun.' And there's always going to be naysayers. Whether it's OnlyFans or some other job I've done, there's always somebody who wants to say something mean. You know, trolls. I just ignore it, honestly."

"I think the stigma around joining OnlyFans has changed," she said. "It's continuing to evolve. It's sort of like a modern-day fan club where you get to be directly with your fans. The content is right there. And especially as women in the entertainment industry, you want to have control over your own image. It's so important. It made total sense for me to join. And I think it's timely for people who want to take control of their own created image and content online."

Eleniak said she's comfortable embracing her sexy side while maintaining control over the content she shares.

"To me, sexy means being confident in your skin, being confident in who you are, as opposed to just the aesthetics of what you look like," she said. "I think sexiness comes from inside and feeling good in your skin. Back in 'Baywatch,' I was so young, and you're just figuring things out in your 20s. But now that I'm in my 50s, I feel like I've got it figured out. I feel sexy and confident in ways that make me feel empowered. I'm having fun and calling the shots."

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"I'm flirty, but I keep it classy and spicy," she said with a laugh.

As Eleniak continues to find success on OnlyFans, she's hoping to make a splash on "Baywatch" once again — decades after hanging up her iconic red swimsuit.

She is set to reprise the role in a guest appearance on Fox's upcoming "Baywatch" reboot, which is scheduled to premiere Jan. 6, 2027.

"I am very excited to be a part of the reboot," she said. "I think it's going to be amazing. I'm definitely hoping they will get picked up for another season and bring me back for a more regular role. I would love that. Looking back, the show was just magic. It was an escape for everybody, no matter where you lived in the world. It's still magic."

item.title: Angel Reese after Atlanta Dream's disappointing WNBA Finals Game 7 loss: 'We'll be back'
item.description: Angel Reese finished Game 7 with eight points and four turnovers, then promised the Atlanta Dream would be back after falling one win short of a WNBA title.
item.content:encoded:
SAN FRANCISCO – Angel Reese is already looking toward another championship run after the Atlanta Dream fell one win short of a title Saturday night.

"It is tough in the moment, but we’ll be back," Reese said after the Dream’s 68-63 loss to the Golden State Valkyries in Game 7 of the WNBA Finals at Chase Center.

ANGEL REESE, ATLANTA DREAM FALL SHORT IN GAME 7 AS GOLDEN STATE VALKYRIES WIN FIRST WNBA CHAMPIONSHIP

Reese finished with eight points on 3-for-7 shooting, 12 rebounds and four turnovers. She scored one point and did not attempt a field goal in the fourth quarter as Golden State secured its first championship.

Gabby Williams scored 28 of her 30 points in the second half and was named Finals MVP. Reese finished a fourth consecutive game with more turnovers than made baskets.

But afterward, Reese said she remained proud of her season and grateful for the teammates who helped Atlanta get within one victory of a championship.

"I’m really proud of the year that I had," Reese said. "I mean, I’ve done a lot of great things this year, but I wouldn’t be able to do it without this group."

"I’m a young player and I’m very vocal, but I think they really helped me a lot mature in different ways that I haven’t really been challenged," Reese said. "And they really challenged me to be better every single day."

Reese described a locker room where players supported one another’s accomplishments.

"There’s no egos in the locker room and nobody’s selfish," she said. "Like, everybody just wants to see each other succeed."

WNBA FINALS TEAMS END SEASON WITH ONE FINAL NATIONAL ANTHEM SNUB AS DREAM, VALKYRIES LEAVE COURT

That, Reese argued, was a reason to believe Atlanta could eventually finish the job.

"When you have a team like that, I’ve been a part of some teams and I know what it takes to win a championship," she said. "And that’s the winning mindset."

Reese won a national championship at LSU in 2023 and was named the Final Four’s Most Outstanding Player. Famously, she taunted Iowa star Caitlin Clark as the clock wound down on her team's victory.

Reese combined for 51 points and 28 rebounds in Atlanta’s victories in Games 2 and 3, helping the team build a 2-1 series lead.

Before Game 4, she spoke about getting into Golden State’s head.

"They’re playing into my mental game where I can take their confidence and just try to do whatever to mess them up," Reese said.

USA SPORTS, NBC CLAIM RECORD WNBA FINALS RATINGS, BUT COMPARISONS LEAVE OUT IMPORTANT CONTEXT

Atlanta lost three of the next four games. Over that stretch, Reese averaged 9.5 points while shooting 12 for 45 (26.7%) and committing 19 turnovers. She continued to rebound, averaging 12.5 per game, but her scoring dropped sharply from the two victories that put Atlanta ahead.

The Dream forced Game 7 behind Allisha Gray and Rhyne Howard’s combined 44 points in Thursday’s 80-69 win. In the deciding game, Atlanta led by nine midway through the third quarter before Williams took over.

Reese’s last field goal came with 2:12 remaining in the third. Her only point in the fourth came at the foul line with 18.6 seconds left.

Following the loss, she spoke about how much she had wanted to win for her teammates and Atlanta’s supporters.

"I love these girls. I love the coaches," Reese said. "I think it also sucks because our fan base back home poured into us so much this year, and we really wanted to do it for them, but we’re forever grateful."

She also expressed enthusiasm about another offseason working with Dream coach Karl Smesko.

"When individually you get better in the offseason, you get better collectively," Reese said, and then added that she was "looking forward to another year under Karl and his development and his system."

"Just because we didn’t win today doesn’t mean that we won’t be champions in the future," she said.

item.title: JONATHAN TURLEY: Pope Leo XIV casts ballot in US election, raising questions about foreign leaders voting
item.description: Pope Leo XIV mailed an absentee ballot to Will County, Illinois, raising novel legal questions about a foreign head of state voting in U.S. elections.
item.content:encoded:
"So, the Pope doesn’t take sides. Prevost has another opinion, but we won’t do that now."

That funny quip from Pope Leo XIV, born Robert Prevost, referred to the historic game in Rome when the Villanova and Notre Dame basketball teams play each other.

However, a story this week raised a different question of when the Pope, as opposed to Prevost, can "take sides."

POPE LEO MEETS WITH CHICAGO'S FAR-LEFT MAYOR, GEORGE FLOYD'S FAMILY LAWYER AT THE VATICAN

This month, American-born Pope Leo XIV became the first pope ever to vote in a U.S. election.

A longtime Chicago native, the Pope mailed an absentee ballot to Will County, and the clerk’s office confirmed to Fox News Digital that "Robert Prevost is on the list of individuals who requested a Vote by Mail ballot."

There is no question that the pope can vote in the Holy See. Indeed, he is the ultimate and final vote in the Vatican, but can he actually vote in Illinois races — including the governor’s race involving incumbent Democrat J.B. Pritzker? The answer appears to be yes, but it raises some novel questions.

Now, as a threshold matter, I want to shed some bias. I was raised Catholic in Chicago. No, that is not the bias. There is that lingering conflict with the pope coming out as a White Sox fan. Many of us on the North Side hoped for a conversion to restore our faith in papal infallibility. However, he has remained entrenched in his South Side allegiance.

This column rises above that historic rivalry and does not suggest that White Sox fans can be challenged at the polls. Besides, I previously explained that the pope is a Cubs fan without knowing it.

CHICAGO MAYOR JOHNSON HOPES TO ENLIST POPE IN REPARATIONS FIGHT AFTER HE APOLOGIZED FOR 'SCOURGE OF SLAVERY'

Rather, what surprised me was that the head of a foreign state could vote in U.S. elections. The Vatican is a distinct nation with a diplomatic corps, a court system, a local government, and even a military in the form of the legendary Swiss Guards.

The Holy See Press Office declared, "Pope Leo XIV has exercised his right to vote as a United States citizen whenever he was eligible to do so. The Holy See Press Office confirms that, in keeping with this long-standing practice of civic participation, he has submitted his mail-in ballot in Chicago."

The Holy See maintains that Pope Leo retains his status as a U.S. citizen while serving as the head of a foreign nation. There is support for this position.

The State Department has maintained that dual citizens do not have to choose between their countries, though it does not expect them to serve as the head of another country.

Notably, the State Department requires dual citizens to use a U.S. passport to enter the country. Does that mean that, when traveling as head of state, Pope Leo has to use a U.S. passport? Unlikely, but intriguing.

It strikes me as odd that a person can lead another country and still vote in U.S. elections. With all of those worried about Russian interference in elections, imagine if Putin could actually vote in U.S. elections. Obviously, Pope Leo is greatly loved and represents someone whose values are aligned with this country. Yet, he is also the head of state of a foreign nation.

SUPREME COURT RULES ON MAIL-IN BALLOTS RECEIVED AFTER ELECTION DAY

Under the Uniformed and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act (UOCAVA), military personnel and citizens abroad are allowed to vote in U.S. elections. It is no longer considered an absentee vote requiring an excuse but simply a mail-in ballot.

The question is whether this right should be suspended when you assume a position in a foreign nation, let alone the head of such a nation. Dual citizenship has long been debated over the difficult questions raised by nations with opposing values and interests. However, being the head of a foreign government with potentially opposing interests and actions to the United States creates a curious status.

STATE DEPARTMENT CONSIDERS SHARING PASSPORT RECORDS FOR VOTER CITIZENSHIP CHECKS

It turns out that when Gov. Pritzker met with the pope last year, he was actually meeting with a constituent and voter.

I am most surprised that the Vatican does not have a policy against such voting, though this is admittedly unprecedented. I would think that the head of the Catholic faith and the head of a foreign government would have a single national citizenship running to the Holy See. All popes are selected from the global faithful by the College of Cardinals and thus have national citizenship with other countries.

In assuming their positions, the cardinals "pledge and swear, as individuals and as a group, to observe faithfully and scrupulously the prescriptions contained in the Apostolic Constitution."

They also reaffirm that they are not subject to countervailing allegiances or pressures from outside the College: "And never to lend support or favour to any interference, opposition or any other form of intervention, whereby secular authorities of whatever order and degree or any group of people or individuals might wish to intervene in the election of the Roman Pontiff."

However, it is fascinating that, once elected, popes do not shed that status upon assuming the head of the Holy See.

It is an uncomfortable question since it also raises whether the head of a foreign government should have dual citizenship. Most people were legitimately thrilled, including myself, by the first American pope and can view this as an unlikely "one-off." However, it could just as easily happen with another nation and a dual citizen.

At the risk of my own excommunication, it seems a worthy question for discussion, even though I doubt any politicians would relish such a debate.

For his part, Pope Leo stated before the Villanova-Notre Dame game that the pope will not take sides in the U.S. elections, but Robert Prevost will.

item.title: Wyoming mom reported missing after not picking up kids; sister, police search for answers
item.description: Kandice Gunter's phone last pinged near Highway 387 in Natrona County after the 30-year-old mother failed to pick up her kids from Boys & Girls Club.
item.content:encoded:
A Wyoming mother of two has been reported missing for days after she failed to pick up her children from an after-school program, prompting her sister to raise the alarm.

Kandice Gunter, 30, was last seen Thursday morning in Natrona County, according to the Casper Police Department. Her sister, Kayla Gunter, told Cowboy State Daily she reported her missing after Kandice did not collect her children, ages 9 and 6, from the Boys & Girls Club on Wednesday.

"That's why I started freaking out," Kayla told the paper. "It's totally out of character for her not to show up to get her kids."

FAMILY OF CRITICALLY MISSING DC MOTHER SAYS POLICE STILL TREATING HOME AS ACTIVE CRIME SCENE

Police said Gunter was last known to be traveling in a gray 2016 GMC Canyon pickup with a Wyoming temporary registration. Her cellphone was last located around 12:30 p.m. MT on Friday along Highway 387, near the Natrona County line.

The sisters last spoke by phone at 10:41 a.m. local time Wednesday. Kayla said the conversation gave no indication anything was wrong, and Gunter stopped answering calls afterward. The family was also told her phone pinged near Gillette around noon Wednesday, according to the report.

Gunter had reportedly moved from Nevada to Casper about a month earlier to be closer to her children. She had been staying with their father and helping care for them.

BAHAMIAN AUTHORITIES APPROVE SEARCH OF 25-FOOT-DEEP ZONE FLAGGED BY BRIAN HOOKER'S PHONE GPS DATA: SOURCES

"I looked so hard but there’s so much wide open spaces with one set of sad eyes hope you’re okay!! 14 years you’ve been in my life and can’t end it like this Kandice Gunter," Facebook user TK Kentopp posted early Saturday morning.

NEW YORK GRANDMOTHER VANISHES IN LAS VEGAS AS FAMILY GETS MYSTERIOUS TEXTS FROM HER PHONE ASKING FOR BITCOIN

In the days before she disappeared, Gunter posted on Facebook: "Success for me, happens in silence." She had also written in June about "focusing on a better me. Again," alongside a heart-mending emoji.

Kayla said the move appeared to be going well and her sister had not indicated she planned to leave or cut off contact. The sisters typically spoke by phone at least three times a day.

Gunter was last seen in person on the morning of Oct. 29 in Natrona County and was reported missing to police later that evening, the Casper Police Department said. She was last known to be traveling in a gray 2016 GMC Canyon pickup with Wyoming temporary registration. Her cellphone was last located along Highway 387, near the Natrona County line, around 12:30 p.m. Friday, Oct. 30.

Gunter is described as 5 feet 7 inches tall and weighing about 185 pounds, with black hair and blue eyes. She has a butterfly tattoo on her neck.

Anyone who has seen Gunter or the pickup, or has information about her whereabouts, is asked to call the Casper Police Department at 307-235-8278. Anonymous tips can be submitted to Crime Stoppers of Central Wyoming at 307-577-8477 or at crimestopperscasper.org.

item.title: Trace Adkins praises pro fishing for embracing faith and patriotism: 'They're not afraid'
item.description: Trace Adkins sang the national anthem at The Champions tournament on Old Hickory Lake, where bass fishing's biggest stars competed for $1.25 million.
item.content:encoded:
NASHVILLE — Country music star Trace Adkins has spent decades entertaining audiences around the world. But on Saturday morning in Tennessee, the roles were reversed, as the longtime outdoorsman found himself a little starstruck by some of the biggest names in professional bass fishing.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

Adkins performed the national anthem before the championship round of World Bass Enterprises' inaugural The Champions tournament on Old Hickory Lake, where 15 of the world's top professional bass anglers were competing for a record $1.25 million first-place prize.

And while the country star was impressed by the talent on the water, he told OutKick OutDoors that he particularly appreciated the sport's willingness to embrace faith and patriotism.

"I'm just thrilled to be here today. Some of the finest anglers on the planet," Adkins said in an exclusive interview. "And, you know, growing up fishing, it's like these guys are rock stars, you know? And to get to shake hands with some of them.

"I like that they're not afraid of God or patriotism. They're going to pray and have the national anthem before they fish."

For Adkins, who grew up in Louisiana and has long been an avid outdoorsman, fishing is much more than a passing hobby.

In fact, he's been celebrating the sport for years.

His 2011 hit "Just Fishin'" tells the story of a father taking his young daughter fishing, capturing the idea that time spent together outdoors is about much more than what's on the end of the line.

That same year, Adkins opened the lake on his Middle Tennessee property to a group from Big Brothers Big Sisters, giving children and their mentors an opportunity to enjoy a day of fishing and other outdoor activities.

And in a 2017 interview with Fox News, the singer joked that he'd found a way to make his fishing trips considerably more productive.

"I don't go on fishing trips anymore," he said at the time. "I stocked my own hole full of fish so I don't fish, I just catch."

ANDY HOUSER OPENS UP ABOUT HIS LIFELONG LOVE OF FISHING AND UNFORGETTABLE TRIP WITH NAVY SEALS

But even with his own stocked fishing hole, Adkins still appreciates the professionals who have helped turn bass fishing into a major spectator sport.

"Oh yeah, I grew up, there was Roland Martin and Bill Dance on television," Adkins said. "You know, they were the only two. When you look at it now, I mean, what it's become, it's just exciting."

And the scale of this weekend's event illustrated just how far the sport has come.

The Champions brought together top competitors from the Bassmaster Elite Series and Major League Fishing's Bass Pro Tour for a three-day competition featuring a $3.25 million total purse — the largest in professional bass fishing history.

The tournament concluded Saturday with Matt Robertson claiming the $1.25 million grand prize, capping off a historic weekend for professional bass fishing.

The event also featured a team competition between the two circuits, with Bassmaster's Team Stars winning The Champions Cup on Friday before the remaining 15 anglers advanced to Saturday's individual championship.

For Adkins, who has enjoyed fishing since childhood, being part of that moment meant getting to celebrate both the sport and the traditions he values.

OutKick OutDoors is on the ground at Old Hickory Lake, bringing readers exclusive interviews, tournament updates and behind-the-scenes coverage of the richest competition in professional bass fishing.

Follow OutKick OutDoors on Instagram, TikTok and YouTube for exclusive interviews, video highlights and coverage of The Champions all weekend long.

item.title: Cops raid West Virginia frat houses in hazing probe as growing crackdown should be ‘wake-up call’: expert
item.description: Police served search warrants at West Virginia University's Lambda Chi Alpha and Pi Kappa Alpha houses amid fraternity hazing investigations.
item.content:encoded:
In the latest in a slew of fraternity hazing investigations nationwide, law enforcement agencies are poring over evidence taken from the Lambda Chi Alpha fraternity house at West Virginia University.

On Oct. 26, blaring music pounded as hundreds of shouting bystanders lined the street and nearby properties of the multi-level, brick, frat house on the Morgantown campus.

Meanwhile, officers with the campus and local police department, armed with a search warrant tied to hazing allegations, stoically toted out bags and cases of evidence and loaded it into police cars.

FOUR FRATERNITY PLEDGES ARRESTED ON HAZING ALLEGATIONS AFTER TEEN FORCED INTO TRUCK: COPS

A little more than two weeks earlier on Oct. 9, the university placed the chapter on interim suspension after "anonymous allegations of hazing," a university spokeswoman told Fox News Digital.

Search warrants also were served on Oct. 26 at the house for the school’s chapter of Pi Kappa Alpha, according to social media posts from WVU Safety and Wellness.

LSU FRAT PLEDGES ALLEGEDLY WATERBOARDED, FORCED TO CHUG MILK IN HAZING RITUALS: REPORT

That fraternity, commonly known as PIKE, also is under investigation for allegations of hazing. As of that date, the university’s PIKE organization had not been put on suspension by the university.

The two West Virginia University chapters are the latest fraternities under investigation in an influx of Greek life hazing probes across the country.

Hazing involves requiring new or potential recruits to the military or college fraternities to perform strenuous, humiliating, or dangerous tasks.

FORMER MICHIGAN HOCKEY PLAYERS ALLEGE COACHES IGNORED YEARS OF ABUSIVE HAZING RITUALS

The uptick in law enforcement involvement nationwide doesn’t necessarily signal an increase in hazing, said Michael Ayalon, hazing prevention expert and CEO of Greek University.

More likely is that there’s increased awareness about hazing, triggered by changes to federal law, Ayalon told Fox News Digital.

MIAMI SECRET SERVICE AGENT CHARGED IN NEAR-DEADLY FRATERNITY HAZING, OFFICIALS SAY

The Stop Campus Hazing Act passed in December 2024 with bipartisan support in Congress. It requires more transparency in hazing allegations across the country, Ayalon said.

"We certainly are seeing increased visibility and scrutiny of hazing on college campuses, particularly as universities face greater expectations for transparency and accountability.

DOZENS OF PLEDGES FOUND COVERED IN FOOD IN SWELTERING FRAT BASEMENT AS POLICE INVESTIGATE ALLEGED HAZING

"With that transparency and accountability comes greater visibility."

But more visibility doesn’t necessarily suggest more hazing is occurring now, he said.

ARIZONA LAWMAKERS DEMAND INDEPENDENT INVESTIGATION INTO ASU HOCKEY WORKOUT THAT LEFT PLAYER IN COMA

Hazing always has been underreported, he said, due to fear of retaliation.

Fraternity members should recognize that public perception of fraternity life now is being affected by these investigations, he said.

"The positive contributions of thousands of fraternity members can get overshadowed by allegations involving a handful of chapters," Ayalon said.

"So every hazing incident makes it harder for the good chapters to go out and recruit more new members, makes it harder for alumni to defend the fraternity experience, and it makes it harder for universities that are working with these organizations."

"For students, I think this is a wake-up call."

Despite decades of education about the dangers of hazing traditions, national policy changes and tragic deaths, "some chapters continue to believe that hazing is a necessary part of earning membership," he said.

It’s based on flawed thinking, he said.

Members justify the abuse, he said, by telling themselves, "I had to go through it, so you have to go through it, too."

Fraternity chapters promote the idea that hazing builds brotherhood and creates loyalty, he said.

SEND US A TIP

"But there is a profound difference between working through a meaningful challenge as equals and being humiliated or controlled by people who hold power over you."

Historically, hazing methods have followed patterns based on the kind of fraternity of sorority involved, Ayalon said.

GOT A TIP?

Fraternities that are traditionally white, known as IFC fraternities, are known for forced alcohol consumption, he said. Eighty-two percent of hazing deaths involve forced alcohol consumption.

In historically white sororities, hazing typically takes a different form, he said. In Panhellenic organizations, hazing looks like mental abuse—mean-girl behavior that ostracizes new female members.

GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL

In historically black fraternities and sororities of the National Pan-Hellenic Council (NPHC) —often called the Divine Nine—abuse may be physical or mental, Ayalon said.

And some recent high-profile cases of hazing have involved drugs, he said.

"West Virginia University takes seriously the safety and well-being of our students," a spokeswoman for West Virginia University said.

"Due to the nature of the investigations, no other details will be released at this time. We will provide updates as they become available."

Fox News Digital reached out to Lambda Chi Alpha and Pi Kappa Alpha for comment.

item.title: 5 habits that could help keep you out of a nursing home, from an orthopedic surgeon
item.description: Dr. Vonda Wright shares five daily habits that help older adults maintain independent living, starting with skeletal longevity and muscle strength.

Three in four Americans aged 50 and older would like to remain in their homes as they age, according to the AARP — and preserving that independence starts with daily habits.

Dr. Vonda Wright, a double board-certified orthopedic surgeon, author and authority on active aging and mobility, who is based in Orlando, Florida, said there are three main problems that can make it difficult for older adults to age in place.

Those include difficulty getting up from a chair and caring for themselves, memory problems, and incontinence that makes it hard to manage personal hygiene.

FORGET THE GYM: A 30-SECOND TEST MAY BE ONE OF THE BEST INDICATORS OF LONGEVITY

"The missing piece in most conversations between mental health, physical health and independence is your skeletal longevity," Wright said.

Staying independent with age requires attention to the entire musculoskeletal system, including the muscles, bones and tendons, according to the surgeon.

Wright shared the following habits as most important for maintaining independence outside of a nursing home.

The human body "craves mobility," Wright said.

"When you think about it, it's our first skill. We learn to walk when we're 1," she pointed out.

WEEKLY WEIGHTLIFTING SWEET SPOT MAY BE LINKED TO LONGER LIFE, STUDY FINDS

For older adults, staying active can help preserve the ability to handle everyday tasks independently. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention suggests low-impact activities such as walking, cycling and water exercise.

"Even when your hips hurt, even when your knees hurt, you should move on the ground, or get in a pool in chest-high water," Wright suggested.

While the doctor does not recommend exercising through a new injury or severe pain, she pushed back against the belief that rest is the best way to address pain.

PEOPLE LIVING PAST 100 IN ONE TINY VILLAGE SHARE 3 DAILY HABITS

"Rest doesn't cure anything. When you have, for instance, arthritic knees, do you know what can help? Building the muscles around your knees, building the muscles in your hips to support your knees," she said. "So rest is not the answer for feeling better — staying strong and mobile is."

Strength training can help older adults maintain the ability to get out of a chair, climb stairs and carry groceries — everyday tasks that support independent living.

There is never an age or skill level when it’s too late to build muscle, according to Wright.

FITNESS EXPERT REVEALS 6 THINGS PEOPLE OVER 35 SHOULD DO AFTER WORKOUTS TO STAY STRONG

"Even if you feel like you've declined or your parents have declined, there is no age or skill level when we can't become more mobile, when we can't build muscle or reconnect the neuromuscular pathways," she said.

It’s even possible to build muscle sitting in a wheelchair, she noted. "Some of the very first research done by Dr. Maria Fiatarone at Tufts University showed that even at 90 years old, you can regain function."

In that small 1990 study, nine nursing home residents who completed eight weeks of high-intensity resistance training increased their muscle strength by an average of 174%, and also showed improvements in muscle size and mobility.

The National Institute on Aging recommends that older adults perform muscle-strengthening activities at least two days a week, targeting all major muscle groups, with recovery time between sessions.

Some options include resistance bands, hand weights and body-weight exercises. Beginners are advised to start gradually and seek guidance from a doctor or physical therapist as needed.

Older adults tend to eat less, which can undermine efforts to maintain energy and build muscle, Wright warned.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

"It’s something I see even happening to my 86-year-old parents; they're just eating less and less," she said. "And we cannot fuel the muscle we want to build [and] the energy we need without a protein-forward, adequate-calorie diet."

Although older adults may require fewer calories, they still need enough nutrients to support their health, according to the National Institute on Aging.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

To help maintain muscle, the agency recommends that older adults consume protein-rich foods throughout the day, including seafood, dairy, fortified soy products, beans and lentils. Specific calorie needs will vary based on each person’s weight and activity level.

Wright urged older adults to challenge assumptions about what they can and can’t do as they age.

"The most common mistake I see seniors making as they age is assuming that aging is an inevitable decline from vitality to frailty," she said.

"They just assume that a certain number of birthday candles predisposes them to sitting on a couch the rest of their life. The reality is that there is no age or skill level when you're done."

Wright suggested that people should start working toward future independence during their busy working years.

"We need to start thinking about that in our busiest times of life, in our 30s, our 40s, our prime times of working," she said. "It’s part of a long-term, lifetime plan to live where you want to live, with whom you want to live, when you want to live there."

The doctor recommends that adults directly ask their aging parents what assistance they need and to explore available support, including community programs.

In many cases, she said, parents do not want to be a burden to their adult children, so they never ask for anything.

"I think this is a time for really open, frank conversations," Wright said. "What do you want help with? How can I help you? How could we get help for you if possible?"

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

As an example, Wright said her elderly parents live with her family. When she noticed their meals started to suffer while she was traveling, she arranged for support to help them continue managing their lives.

"I have half of their meals delivered every week because I'm not going to be home to shop or cook," she said. "They remain independent, but with assistance. And that's what works for us."
